captions.Library-Akkadian-Merchant:
When Ashur-Muttabil died, things were bad. With no food and no money, with her husband's family against her, Kunnaniya didn't think that she would survive. “I'm going to die,” she wrote to her sister. But then an opportunity arose. A small one, a single bolt of cloth to be traded. Then another, then another. She took each one.

Today, it is not her husband that leads caravans from Kanesh to Assur, it is her sons. One of her daughters supervises the weavers and artisans. The other is a high priestess of Anna. Kunnaniya herself presides over her records: the contracts, the trades, the accounts, the letters... and that final, precious message from Ashur-Muttabil: “Cheer up your heart.”
captions.Library-Aksum-Man:
The boy has just come running, excited to be the first to bear the news: the caravan from Adulis is on its way. Za-Walda hopes it carries plenty of Indian steel—there is never enough of it to go round.

And cotton. Good Indian cotton cloth is superior to the finest Egyptian linen. It will be snatched up before it even reached Alexandria. As long as Mäkwännät manages to procure the ivory she promised for the exchange, they will both profit well from this trade.
captions.Library-Aksum-Woman:
Mäkwännät is worried. She has seen the boy running to Za-Walda's shop and can guess what it was about: the caravan with goods from India is on its way. She has buyers lined up in Myos Hormos. Some of them swore they could sell every scrap as far as Rome. But first she needs ivory for the exchange, and the shipment is late.

Well, in the worst case she would call in favours from a few people she knew and get the ivory she needed. She was an Axumite, after all, and a trader. Things like this did not even slow her down.
captions.Library-Alexandria:
She could have strangled the copyist. It is clear that he didn't understand the Conics, but that's understandable. Apollonius is hardly easy, and Berenike knows no-one apart from herself who can really follow the mathematics.

No, the problem is that the copyist clearly got bored and skipped words and whole sentences. Here, look at proposition twelve: that point has to lie outside the parabola, otherwise the proposition is nonsensical.

Good thing she is here to fix it.
captions.Library-Angkor-Wat:
“Do not cling.” He has had to repeat the Enlightened One's admonition to himself several times already. But even a monk of his standing can be forgiven a little excitement.

Manuscripts have started to arrive from Lanka lately. New manuscripts, dealing with ancient matters. But they are written in Pāli, and only a handful of monks here can read them properly. Sovann has heard about Moggallāna's Pāli thesaurus for more than a year, but never hoped to see a copy. Now it lies in front of him. It is itself written in Pāli, true, and in the rounded script used in Lanka, not in the familiar Khmer. It won't be easy, but what is? “Do not cling.” His fingers itch to start the work.
captions.Library-Celtic-Comic:
Tribute from the southern farms: 18 cattle, 11 cattle hides, 23 goat hides, 7 jars of honey. Bronze torcs delivered: six. Paid for: four. Men owing ale for the midsummer feast: see next tablet.

Gobannos still hasn't delivered the four spearheads he was making. Brennos hopes he hasn't gone on another bender. The smith is mostly dependable, but he does have a taste for Italian wine.

And, by Toutatis, Cunomoltus still has not returned the spear he borrowed. He'll have to speak to him about that.
captions.Library-Contemporary-Amhara:
Hanna Tesfaye pushes up the sleeves of her dress to give herself more freedom of movement. All these returns have to be shelved, and she needs to check what's outstanding. Biruk is probably late again—a sweet boy, but he forgets to return his books.

Hanna is well aware that the Wollo dress she is wearing is not practical for her work in the library. Her mother tells her so all the time. But she likes to look good, and the dress is lovely.
captions.Library-Death:
Number eleven trillion, two hundred and seven billion, three hundred seventy eight thousand, four hundred and four. Deceased on schedule. Archive and close the file.

Number eleven trillion, two hundred and seven billion, three hundred seventy eight thousand, four hundred and five—alive, against all odds. Open a review ticket.

Number eleven trillion, two hundred and seven billion, three hundred seventy eight thousand, four hundred and six. Deceased...
captions.Library-Dragon:
Raouwa Da Horouwe Ra Mha (“The bright-eyed one who is as light as a daisy”—dragon parents are long-winded, but they do dote on their children) used to have a hoard of gold like any other self-respecting dragon. But lying on a pile of gold, waiting for the next metal-clad nitwit to come gallumphing around quickly got boring. So she started buying books: first one, then two, then as many as the eager merchants could drag up her mountain.

Now the gold is gone, but she doesn't mind. In fact, she considers this her best decision since the time she decided not to eat that frightened girl the bishop offered, but snacked on the fat bishop instead. To be fair, her archival skills leave much to be desired. She once spent a month looking for a book that turned up in a well-chewed helmet of a long-forgotten knight.
captions.Library-Gondar:
Abba Täklä Haymanot does not want to get drawn into the debate. Was Christ anointed by the very union of divinity and humanity, or was the Holy Spirit the unction? An important question, but is it really given to mortal men to understand the answer? That confidence seems arrogant, even faintly blasphemous to him.

He knows better than to speak his doubts, though, so he deflects questions and claims that he is too busy with his chronicle of the reign of Fasilides to give the question its proper consideration. It even happens to be true.
captions.Library-Hermit:
The last time Luc went down to La Rencontre, Alain made it his business to mock his library. He had the nerve to ask, of all things, if he planned to use the books for kindling when winter came around. It was all Luc could do to restrain himself or they might have come to blows.

Now he prefers to stay here and read. Books are better company than Alain any day, and beer at La Rencontre was watery stuff anyway.
captions.Library-Inca:
The court has gone back to Cusco, and Waman Qispi is not unhappy to see them go. His reverence for the Sapa Inka is undiminished, it will not suffer from a little distance. But some of the courtiers… well, they undoubtedly have high matters of state to deal with and can hardly be expected to know the difference between a pack-knot and a khipu.

Waman does know. He does not need to be asked three times in a row if he is sure the stores of maize were sufficient for the season. They are, because he has made sure of it.
captions.Library-Khumbu:
A group of trekkers came up from Namche in the afternoon and asked if they could spend the night. Tenzing Norbu does not mind, as long as they stay in the guest rooms and take off their boots. Their donations will help pay for the monastery's upkeep. Perhaps they will buy a thangka. Meanwhile, he has to go down to the village while there is daylight left and buy rice. He can't let Pumba negotiate with the trader, or he'd get swindled again. And he has to check in on Tsomo's daughter who wis running a fever. If her aunt's tea hasn't made her better, it might be time to take her to the clinic.

Sometimes he wonders how things might have been if he'd studied in one of the famous Indian monasteries instead of Tengboche. But he is too busy to dwell on might-have-beens.
captions.Library-Lego: Legos. You try to keep track of them!
captions.Library-Maori-Pa:
Things are changing. Pakeha have been coming in increasing numbers in their oversized waka, mostly up north, but they have visited her pā as well. Inquisitive and awkward, but mostly respectful, so far. Hinewaiora even acquired two of their pukapuka. They are strange. They contain words without having a voice to speak them. How can one know then which words are true and which are not?

Mists gather outside and she, rangatira, stands on the threshold, bound by whakapapa to her ancestors, by duty to her people.
captions.Library-Maya-Tikal: Unless something extraordinary happens, K’in Lakam Chahk will have to go without cacao for a while. Everyone knows that the Seven Temples team, with Yax B'alam to lead them, is unbeatable—everyone but Chak Tok' who will support the palace team until his last breath. So K'in was happy to take Chak's bet on today's game and even raised it to seven measures of cacao beans. Then Yax went an injured his knee, and now certain victory is starting to look like certain defeat and K'in has been cursing himself all day. He does like his cacao.
captions.Library-Medieval-Europe-Illumination:
Brother Anselm is certain that young Brother Godric is the culprit, but he knows that asking if anyone saw anything would be a waste of time. Last night before vespers, he had just started a fresh vellum leaf—stretched and rubbed with pumice, ruled, but otherwise blank. Today, right after matins, the first page was half-filled with an illumination, a rendering of this very scriptorium and him, Anselm, working at the lectern. Even if Godric had accomplices, as he must have had, it was impressive work for one night. And a good likeness too, Anselm had to admit.

He would be more flattered if he knew how he was supposed to explain the whole thing to the abbot.
captions.Library-Paleolithic:
Ever since Mengei O was little, she has liked to keep things organized. As a little girl, she would make piles of similar pebbles. She would stack similar twigs, she'd recite all the words for mushrooms that she knew to eye-rolling adults and ask if there were any others.

Now she is old. She has seen more than thirty winters, more than anyone but old Gnodu. And now eager children come to her, to show off their knowledge, to recite names for things they know and to ask endless questions. She is glad to answer.
captions.Library-Pompidou:
Next week, the Bibliothèque publique d’information is going to move out of the building for the first time since 1977. The Centre Pompidou needs renovation and the library is moving to the 12e arrondissement. Which means—Claire Moreau holds her breath for a heartbeat, then lets it out slowly—which means that dozens of packers will descend on the library to pack up the books, drive them across the city to the Lumière building and re-shelve them. Left to their own devices, they would probably create a mess that no-one would ever untangle.

Well, that's what she is here for.
captions.Library-Samarkand:
This new student, Zhang Mingyuan, is… unusual. Shams ad-Din Samarqandi was not accustomed to being confused by a mere student, but he had to admit he was.

The young man arrived two days ago from Khanbaliq in the east, asking to be admitted, but with no letter of recommendation. So Shams gave him an easy test: find the time of the next lunar eclipse. The young man arrived at the answer quicker than Shams thought possible, so he dug deeper: which of Euclid's propositions did he apply in the calculation. He expected a more refined application of geometric principles, or a new method of reduction. What he did not expect was a blank stare: Zhang Mingyuan, it turns out, had never heard of Euclid. Strange indeed.
captions.Library-Shinto-Japan: Matsuda Reiko-sama has asked for the old records to be brought out. Mizunomori no Kami must be moved: the damage to the shrine from the autumn storm was just too severe and repairs will take some time. The sengū has not been performed at this shrine in her lifetime. She could ask one of the junior priests to check the correct steps of the ritual, but the young can be careless. As gūji she is responsible for making sure that everything is done correctly, so she settles down for a few hours of careful reading.
captions.Library-Somme:
Shells have been falling without pause for days. No doubt historians will one day call this the Battle of the Somme, and be all pompous about it. The lads have different names: slaughter-house. Butchery. Hell.

Andy MacLeod wishes he knew which genius decided to put the battalion records in this dugout just off the main trench. Scratch that—he knows exactly whose idea it was. But someone has to make sure the lads get rations, those that can still swallow. Boots, those that can still walk. Bullets, those that can still shoot.

He keeps working. Shells keep falling.
captions.Library-Squirrel:
Ok, berries, check. Nuts, check. More berries, check. Who left those nuts out in the open? Was it me?

What about those berries? Should I be storing them? Do berries survive winter?

What is winter, anyway?
captions.Library-Steampunk:
The new automaton is wonderful. The old ones were large, clanging and steam-powered, which left every page in the library damp and prone to mildew. Yousuf d'Oc has been trying to sell the library one of his automatons for a while, but no-one in her right mind would let a phlogiston-powered machine anywhere near a book. Besides, why would she need all that power?

But this, this was one of the new electrick ones: quick, small and it hardly made a sound as it shelved the books.

Plus—Beatrice DeVale permitted herself a smirk—its arachnid shape frightened the living daylights out of Mr. London and kept him well away from the stacks.
captions.Library-Sumer:
In his youth, Ur-Nana was chosen to be lugal. He performed the rites, he assembled the men, he had the chariots made ready and he led the army in the field, where he performed acts of heroism that poets would sing about for generations. Three times he was called, three times he went and returned victorious. Three times he returned to a city that was on the verge of starvation, where grain records were poorly kept, where temple donations were late, where labourers were close to revolt because their rations had not been issued.

The fourth time he let the honour go to a younger man and instead took it upon him to care for the city. Now his work is in the records and in the temples, not on the battleground, and the city is prospering.
captions.Library-Timbuktu:
Ahmad has been nagging to borrow his copy of Jamʿ al-jawāmiʿ for weeks. Ibrahim ag Moussa knows that he is going to succumb and lend it to the lad. After all, knowledge is not his to hoard, and Ahmad is genuinely interested in the fine points of qiyās.

But Ibrahim also knows what students do to margins. This very copy still bears the scars he himself inflicted on it when he was a young aspiring student of law. He sighs. Better get it over with.

“Ahmad! Come here.”
captions.Library-Trade-Spaceship:
Liset was born on the Arcturus line. She was six before she orbited her first planet, eleven before she set foot on one, and promptly decided that planets are dirty, smelly, unpredictable and overrated. And they have weather, of all things. Who ever came up with an air circulation system that has hurricanes?

It is hard enough to keep a ship running. Sure, most of the work is done by Pippa the Pilot (the AI hates that nickname, so she uses it as much as she can), but it still needs a human touch now and then.
captions.Library-Varro:
Marcus Terentius Varro was once a tribune of the people, a general to Pompeius Magnus, a librarian to Iulius Caesar. He might even have become consul but for his unfortunate habit of speaking his mind. Now Pompeius is dead by Caesar's hand, Caesar by the hand of Marcus Brutus, Brutus by the hand of Marcus Antonius, and who knows if Antonius will survive the ambitions of young Octavianus. And he, Varro, is old.

Old, but not dead. Lately, he has had people call him a greater thinker than Cicero. They flatter, but if that is not the apex of cursus honorum, what is? He gives his already-sharp stylus a final touch-up and begins: “De re rustica...”
captions.Library-Yongle:
Liu Shun misses Nanjing. No question, this new Forbidden City that the Son of Heaven had caused to be built is beautiful. But Nanjing was alive and vibrant. Chaotic—a welcome contrast to the orderly archives that he keeps. This new city is just one magnificent palace after another, all looking the same, until they start to blur before your eyes. There isn't even anywhere decent to go see a play in the evening and have a cup of wine.

He wishes he could have stayed back in Nanjing. But what the emperor commands, Liu Shun does. It has always been so.
